script.text: The fortified crossing and town gate remain visible behind the column as the sortie moves toward Margny.
We hit them, we make space, we come back through there.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Exactly. Don't improve the plan after we leave the gate.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: CH04-B02 — The Gate at Compiègne.

nodes.title: The Gate at Compiègne
nodes.summary: A sortie against the Burgundian siege pressure turns into a fighting retreat. Jeanne and d’Aulon remain with the rear guard as the route to the fortified crossing is lost. The objective changes honestly from attack to retreat to survival; Jeanne is captured by Burgundian forces connected to John of Luxembourg's command.

beats.title: Strike and Return
beats.screenAction: The sortie attacks Burgundian pressure near Margny with a limited goal: disrupt the position and return before reinforcements can seal the route.
beats.dialogueIntent: Start with an achievable limited objective, not a doomed battle disguised as a normal victory map.
beats.result: The forward action disrupts the immediate position, but Burgundian reinforcements begin appearing on the flanks.

script.text: Objective: disrupt the Burgundian forward position, then preserve a route back to Compiègne.
The first Burgundian line gives ground, but movement appears beyond the flank where the sortie did not expect another full body of troops.
That's enough. Back to the town before this becomes their battle.
script.speaker: Jean d’Aulon

beats.title: The Retreat Narrows
beats.screenAction: Reinforcements press the sortie back. Jeanne and d’Aulon remain near the rear while other units stream toward the fortified crossing.
beats.dialogueIntent: Make the capture emerge from a collapsing retreat, not from a cutscene that ignores a successful map objective.
beats.result: The offensive objective is abandoned and the player must preserve the withdrawal corridor.

script.text: Objective changes: RETREAT TO COMPIÈGNE. Keep the route open for the withdrawing force.
Go! I'm behind you!
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: That sentence has never made me feel better.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: The retreat compresses toward the fortified crossing while Burgundian troops press between scattered rear groups.

beats.title: Cut Off
beats.screenAction: The rear guard loses practical access to the crossing. MC tries to reach Jeanne, but Burgundian troops split the field and the available path closes faster than the party can reopen it.
beats.dialogueIntent: The player is allowed to try. The game then states plainly when the rescue route is no longer achievable in this encounter.
beats.result: Jeanne and d’Aulon are isolated with a small rear group; MC's side is forced away from the capture point.

script.text: Objective changes: REACH JEANNE. A rescue route is still visible but collapsing.
A fresh Burgundian push cuts across the last open lane between MC and the rear guard.
Jeanne!
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Jeanne turns once, still fighting toward the crossing with d’Aulon close beside her. The distance grows instead of shrinking.
Rescue route lost. Objective changes: WITHDRAW SURVIVORS. The encounter no longer presents Jeanne's extraction as achievable.

beats.title: The Maid Taken
beats.screenAction: From beyond the severed route, MC sees Jeanne pulled from her horse and taken. d’Aulon is captured with the remaining rear group. The surviving party must leave before it is surrounded as well.
beats.dialogueIntent: End on an earned failure state. John of Luxembourg enters through the custody chain, not as a theatrical personal captor.
beats.result: Jeanne and d’Aulon are prisoners; MC's party survives outside the capture and can begin tracking where they are taken.

script.text: Across the broken retreat, Burgundian soldiers drag Jeanne from her horse and close around the remaining rear guard. d’Aulon disappears into the same knot of prisoners.
We can't reach her from here.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Then we find where they take her.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Complete the withdrawal with surviving required units. No victory banner is shown for Jeanne's capture.
CH04-N06 — Taken.

nodes.title: Taken
nodes.summary: The survivors learn that Jeanne has entered the Burgundian custody chain associated with John of Luxembourg. An immediate battlefield rescue is no longer possible, so the chapter turns from campaigning to tracking a prisoner.

beats.title: No Victory Screen
beats.screenAction: The survivors regroup far enough from Compiègne to stop running. Nobody celebrates surviving the map.
beats.dialogueIntent: Let the failure remain emotionally and mechanically legible.
beats.result: MC accepts that the immediate battle is over and that a different kind of pursuit must begin.

script.text: The group stops only when Compiègne's bells are too far away to hear clearly.
We left her.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: We were cut away from her. Those aren't the same words.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

script.text: They feel the same right now.
script.speaker: MC

beats.title: Follow the Prisoner
beats.screenAction: A report identifies Jeanne as a high-value Burgundian prisoner associated with John of Luxembourg's forces. MC stops thinking in terms of rejoining the campaign and starts thinking in terms of finding her.
beats.dialogueIntent: Turn the saga from campaign adventure into personal rescue pressure without pretending the party can immediately storm the captors.
beats.result: Chapter 4 ends with Jeanne captive, d’Aulon also taken, and MC's group committed to tracking the custody chain.

script.text: The Burgundians are moving the Maid under guard. Luxembourg's people have custody.
script.speaker: Messenger

script.text: Where?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Not somewhere we can reach tonight.
script.speaker: Messenger

script.text: Then tomorrow starts with finding out where.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: CHAPTER 4 COMPLETE
Next: Chapter 5 — Rouen.

nodes.title: The Prisoner's Road
nodes.summary: Months of rumor and paid information replace battlefield maps. Jeanne remains in Burgundian custody before being transferred to the English for a large payment and brought to Rouen. MC's party follows the chain rather than inventing an army that can simply take her back.

beats.title: A Moving Prison
beats.screenAction: The party tracks contradictory reports as Jeanne is moved through Burgundian custody. Leads arrive late, routes change, and every castle rumor is already old by the time they reach it.
beats.dialogueIntent: Replace open-field campaign certainty with frustrating information work.
beats.result: The party learns that direct pursuit is failing and begins following the political custody chain instead.

script.text: Summer 1430
A map fills with names that mean very little by the time the party reaches them. Jeanne is moved faster than reliable news.
Every answer is two days old.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Then stop chasing the last door she passed through. Find who decides the next one.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

beats.title: Sold to the English
beats.screenAction: The party confirms that the English have acquired Jeanne from the Burgundian custody chain for a large ransom-equivalent payment and are taking her toward Rouen.
beats.dialogueIntent: Keep John of Luxembourg and the transfer political and transactional rather than melodramatic personal villainy.
beats.result: Rouen becomes the fixed destination and the first reliable place where the party can plan ahead of the prisoner rather than behind her.

script.text: Luxembourg's custody is ending. The English paid for her transfer.
script.speaker: Informant

script.text: You can buy a person?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: You can call it ransom, transfer, custody, law, politics. She still ends up behind another locked door.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Where?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Rouen.
script.speaker: Informant

beats.title: No Army This Time
beats.screenAction: The group reduces what it carries and plans for a hostile city controlled by the English. A marching army would end the attempt before it starts.
beats.dialogueIntent: Make the genre shift explicit: information, access, and escape routes matter more than battlefield strength.
beats.result: The party approaches Rouen as a small covert group rather than as a formal French force.

script.text: So what is the plan?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: For once? Don't arrive looking like an army.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: CH05-B01 — A Road into Rouen.

nodes.title: A Road into Rouen
nodes.location: Road and river approaches outside Rouen
nodes.summary: Fantasia fictional adaptation: the party escorts a local contact carrying legitimate trade papers through a patrol sweep so they can enter Rouen without inventing a recorded historical rescue battle. The objective is access and survival, not defeating the English garrison.

beats.title: The Papers Matter More
beats.screenAction: A local contact has papers that can place part of the group inside Rouen, but a patrol sweep closes across the approach before they reach the gate traffic.
beats.dialogueIntent: Frame the fictional operation around access. Killing the patrol is neither necessary nor desirable.
beats.result: The party protects the contact and identifies a route around the patrol's main cordon.

script.text: Fantasia adaptation. Objective: protect the contact and reach the trade road without raising a full alarm.
If those papers tear, we get to explain ourselves to every guard in Rouen.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: So for once the paper is the important fighter.
script.speaker: MC

beats.title: Break Contact
beats.screenAction: The group uses terrain and traffic to separate from the patrol instead of turning the approach into an open battle that would close the city to them.
beats.dialogueIntent: Reward restraint and route control, fitting the smaller Rouen chapter scale.
beats.result: The patrol loses a clean line on the group and the contact keeps the gate approach viable.

script.text: Objective update: BREAK CONTACT. Reach the marked route with the contact; unnecessary pursuit risks locking the party out of Rouen.
Hangaku pins the patrol behind cover long enough for carts and pedestrians to close the sightline.
Move. Being memorable is the opposite of the plan.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

beats.title: Inside
beats.screenAction: The papers and contact get part of the group through ordinary gate traffic. Weapons are concealed or left with the outer support team as planned.
beats.dialogueIntent: End with access gained, not an implausible military victory over Rouen.
beats.result: The party establishes a small covert presence inside Rouen and can begin observing the prison and trial structure.

script.text: The gate closes behind a cart. MC is already inside the city when the patrol finally reaches the road outside.
I prefer battles where the enemy doesn't know we won anything.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: CH05-N03 — Rouen.

nodes.title: Rouen
nodes.summary: The party discovers the basic structure they are actually fighting: Jeanne is held in the English castle under military guard while Pierre Cauchon directs the ecclesiastical proceedings. Warwick matters as the English castle/security authority; Bedford's larger regime is background rather than a mandatory personal meeting.

beats.title: The Castle
beats.screenAction: The group maps ordinary traffic around the English castle and learns that Jeanne is held under English military guard rather than in a normal church prison.
beats.dialogueIntent: Make the physical rescue problem concrete before the trial scenes begin.
beats.result: The party identifies the castle as the custody site and understands why a simple prison break is difficult.

script.text: From a rented upper room, the party watches shifts change around the English castle and writes down nothing that would survive a search.
Military guards. Castle doors. Controlled visitors. That isn't an ordinary church prison.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Can we reach her?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Eventually isn't the same answer as safely.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

beats.title: The Trial Has a Shape
beats.screenAction: Through public movement and overheard official business, the party identifies Pierre Cauchon as the bishop directing the case and Warwick as a major English authority over the castle environment. They do not gain private access to either man.
beats.dialogueIntent: Introduce only the named authorities needed for the next conflict; avoid a villain roll-call.
beats.result: The party separates judicial pressure from military custody and realizes disrupting one does not automatically solve the other.

script.text: Clerks move between the castle and church offices under guard. The same two names recur in different conversations: Cauchon for the case, Warwick for the English castle authority around it.
So even if the trial stopped, the soldiers would still have her.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: And opening a cell doesn't make the city gates disappear.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: CH05-N04 — Questions and Chains.

nodes.title: Questions and Chains
nodes.summary: Jeanne's public examinations begin on 21 February under Cauchon's authority. The story presents the pressure of questioning, custody, and isolation without translating her religious claims into Fracture cosmology.

beats.title: First Public Examination
beats.screenAction: On 21 February Jeanne is brought before Cauchon and a large body of assessors in the castle chapel. The scene focuses on pressure, procedure, and Jeanne's refusal to hand over every private conviction on demand.
beats.dialogueIntent: Preserve religious ambiguity. Her voices are her claims and faith experience; the narrative does not re-label them as Fracture messages.
beats.result: The player sees the trial as an escalating institutional danger separate from the physical prison problem.

script.text: Rouen Castle — 21 February 1431
Jeanne stands before Cauchon, clerks, and rows of assessors in the royal chapel. Every answer is being written down.
You will swear to answer truthfully to what is asked of you.
script.speaker: Pierre Cauchon

script.text: I will tell the truth about what concerns me. There are things I won't tell you.
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: The clerks continue writing. The questioning does not end with one refusal.

beats.title: Outside the Room
beats.screenAction: MC cannot simply attend every proceeding. The group reconstructs what it can from public sessions, clerks, servants, guards, and city rumor while continuing to study prison access.
beats.dialogueIntent: Keep MC's access earned and partial. The historical trial remains larger than the protagonist's viewpoint.
beats.result: The party finds one fragile service route that may allow a brief covert meeting but not a full extraction.

script.text: We know when food moves. We know when two guard shifts overlap badly. That isn't enough for a rescue.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Is it enough to see her?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Once. Briefly. If nobody gets ambitious.
script.speaker: Local Contact

script.text: That warning feels targeted.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: CH05-N05 — Through the Bars.

nodes.title: Through the Bars
nodes.location: Rouen Castle — service corridor near Jeanne's cell
nodes.summary: Fantasia fictional adaptation: using a narrow service-access opportunity, MC reaches Jeanne for a brief covert reunion. The meeting gives no magical answer and no easy rescue; Jeanne is exhausted, guarded, and still capable of making her own choices.

beats.title: One Minute Too Long
beats.screenAction: The party uses a service movement window to place MC near Jeanne's cell while Julie watches the corridor. The route is too exposed to move a prisoner through it.
beats.dialogueIntent: Make the reunion costly and limited before it becomes emotional.
beats.result: MC reaches speaking distance of Jeanne but has no viable extraction path.

script.text: Fantasia adaptation. This covert meeting is fictional connective story, not a claim of a recorded historical prison visit.
A service door closes behind MC. Julie remains at the corner where she can see the guard route but not Jeanne's cell.
One minute. Two if every guard in Rouen suddenly becomes stupid.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

beats.title: Still Jeanne
beats.screenAction: MC and Jeanne see each other through the secured cell boundary. Jeanne is worn down by confinement and questioning but refuses to become a passive object in MC's rescue fantasy.
beats.dialogueIntent: Reunite them as friends. Jeanne can be afraid and tired while still retaining agency, faith, and judgment.
beats.result: MC promises to keep looking for a real way out; Jeanne makes MC promise not to throw away everyone else on an impossible rush.

script.text: Rookie?
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: Yes.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: You look terrible.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: You crossed half of France to tell me that?
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: No. I came to get you out.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Then find a road that doesn't kill everyone who follows you through it.
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: I will.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Good. And don't let them turn what I believe into whatever story is easiest for them.
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

beats.title: The Door Closes
beats.screenAction: The guard rhythm changes early and the group abandons the service route before it is exposed. The meeting proves Jeanne is reachable, but not yet extractable.
beats.dialogueIntent: End with a concrete problem to solve rather than false hope.
beats.result: The party begins planning a more dangerous extraction attempt while the trial continues.

script.text: A bootstep sounds where the contact said there should be none. Julie signals once.
Time.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: MC leaves before the corridor can become a trap. The cell door never opened.
CH05-B02 — The Failed Extraction.

nodes.title: The Failed Extraction
nodes.summary: Fantasia fictional adaptation: with Jeanne's danger now immediate, the party attempts a limited extraction through a mapped service route. Security closes faster than expected; the attempt fails causally and the objective changes to preserving the surviving rescue team and its final outside route rather than pretending Jeanne was freed.

beats.title: Reach the Inner Route
beats.screenAction: The party enters through the one service route it has mapped and tries to reach the inner corridor before the next guard rotation.
beats.dialogueIntent: Treat this as a desperate covert extraction, not an invented siege of Rouen Castle.
beats.result: The team reaches the inner approach but discovers that security has tightened beyond the earlier pattern.

script.text: Fantasia adaptation. Objective: reach the inner service corridor before the guard rotation closes.
Same path as before. Faster. Quieter.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Those requirements are fighting each other.
script.speaker: MC

beats.title: The Route Is Gone
beats.screenAction: A reinforced guard movement seals the corridor needed to reach Jeanne's cell, while another patrol begins closing the route behind the party.
beats.dialogueIntent: Fail the extraction because the physical route becomes untenable, not because a cutscene arbitrarily cancels a successful objective.
beats.result: Jeanne's cell is no longer reachable in this attempt and the rescue team risks being trapped inside the castle.

script.text: A reinforced guard group takes the inner turn before the party reaches it. A second lantern line appears behind them.
We can force that door.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: And then fight the castle with nowhere to take her. No.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Extraction route failed. Objective changes: WITHDRAW. Preserve the team and the outside support route.

beats.title: Leave Before the Gates Close
beats.screenAction: The party fights only enough to reopen its exit and breaks away before a full castle alarm traps everyone inside Rouen.
beats.dialogueIntent: The attempt fails, but preserving the rescue team leaves one final desperate option for the next chapter.
beats.result: The party escapes without Jeanne. Its covert prison route is burned and ordinary extraction plans are exhausted.

script.text: Objective: reach the outer safe point with all required rescue-team units.
Hangaku covers the last crossing while Bradamante forces a blocked service gate just far enough for the group to pass.
She is still in there.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Yes. And if we stay, so are we.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: CH05-N07 — Thirty May.

nodes.title: Thirty May
nodes.summary: The party learns that Jeanne is to be taken to the Vieux-Marché that morning. The prison route is gone and ordinary rescue planning has failed. Chapter 5 ends before the stake rescue itself, handing the final attempt to the Finale without revealing what follows a successful rescue.

beats.title: No More Time
beats.screenAction: Before sunrise the contact brings the news the party feared: Jeanne is to be taken out for execution that morning.
beats.dialogueIntent: Collapse the remaining timetable without beginning the Finale early.
beats.result: The group understands that there will be no second prison extraction attempt.

script.text: Rouen — 30 May 1431, before dawn
They're moving her this morning. Vieux-Marché.
script.speaker: Local Contact

script.text: Nobody asks what the sentence means. They all know.
Our prison route is finished.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

script.text: Then we stop planning for the prison.
script.speaker: MC

beats.title: One Last Attempt
beats.screenAction: The group abandons every remaining assumption about a clean extraction and prepares to intercept the execution movement itself. The scene ends before they reach Jeanne or the stake.
beats.dialogueIntent: Hand cleanly into the Finale. Do not reveal the later world-like call, unknown antagonist, or Fracture before the rescue succeeds.
beats.result: Chapter 5 ends with the final rescue attempt beginning; the supernatural turn remains unrevealed.

script.text: This isn't a good plan.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: No.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Just checking.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: We reach her. We free her. Then we find a way out.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Julie checks her sword. Hangaku tightens her bowstring. Bradamante lifts her lance. Dawn begins to reach the rooftops.
CHAPTER 5 COMPLETE
Next: Finale — The Broken Horizon.

nodes.title: Vieux-Marché
nodes.summary: The party follows Jeanne toward the expected execution point and commits to one final rescue. They still know nothing about any larger rule governing her fate; this is a personal choice made because ordinary plans have run out.

beats.title: The Procession
beats.screenAction: Crowds compress the streets around Vieux-Marché while Jeanne is moved under guard. MC’s group stays split among ordinary movement until they can see the custody route clearly.
beats.dialogueIntent: Keep the opening human and immediate. Nobody knows a cosmic event is coming; the only goal is reaching Jeanne before the execution proceeds.
beats.result: The party identifies Jeanne’s route and the last usable approach through the crowd.

script.text: Rouen — 30 May 1431, morning
Crowds press toward Vieux-Marché. English guards move Jeanne through the square while the party keeps to separate edges of the street.
Once we move, there's no clean way back.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: There hasn't been one for a while.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Then choose the moment. Don't let the crowd choose it for you.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

script.text: MC catches sight of Jeanne between two moving lines of guards.
There.
script.speaker: MC

beats.title: The Moment
beats.screenAction: The outer lane is still open, but the guard formation is tightening around Jeanne. Waiting any longer improves the guards’ position rather than the party’s.
beats.dialogueIntent: Turn the chapter handoff into a clear voluntary commitment, not a surprise encounter or miracle opening.
beats.result: The party commits to the rescue and moves before the outer lane closes.

script.text: West lane's still open.
script.speaker: Bradamante

script.text: For how long?
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Long enough if we stop talking.
script.speaker: Bradamante

script.text: We reach Jeanne. Then we get out.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: FIN-B01 — Before the Fire.

nodes.title: Before the Fire
nodes.summary: The final human rescue succeeds through explicit phases: reach Jeanne, free Jeanne, then escape the execution point. The victory is real; the story does not revoke it in a cutscene. Jeanne survives the point where the expected ending says she should die.

beats.title: Reach Jeanne
beats.screenAction: The party breaks from the crowd and opens one narrow route toward Jeanne. The goal is contact, not defeating every guard in the square.
beats.dialogueIntent: Make the first phase focused and legible: one road to Jeanne, with the group covering different pressures rather than becoming an army.
beats.result: The party reaches the custody ring around Jeanne.

script.text: Objective: REACH JEANNE. Defeating every guard is not required.
Don't spread out. We only need one road to her.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Then make it ours.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Hangaku suppresses one side of the route while Bradamante forces space on the other. MC and Julie push toward Jeanne.

beats.title: Free Jeanne
beats.screenAction: The party reaches Jeanne. The objective changes immediately from approach to freeing her and preserving the retreat lane.
beats.dialogueIntent: Let the reunion land quickly without stopping the battle for a long speech.
beats.result: Jeanne is freed from immediate custody and can move with the party.

script.text: Objective update: FREE JEANNE and keep the retreat lane open.
Rookie?
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: Yeah.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: You came.
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: Of course I came.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Reunion later. Move.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Jeanne is pulled clear of the immediate custody line while the outer escape lane is still barely open.

beats.title: Escape the Square
beats.screenAction: With Jeanne free, the party stops trying to control the square and fights only for enough space to move her beyond the execution point. Once they clear it, an impossible distant tone begins beneath the ordinary noise of Rouen.
beats.dialogueIntent: The rescue must genuinely succeed before the supernatural turn. Let the first strange sound arrive only after Jeanne is safely beyond the expected execution point.
beats.result: Jeanne survives the expected execution point. The party clears the square, and a strange world-like call begins from somewhere beyond it.

script.text: Objective update: ESCAPE THE SQUARE with Jeanne.
You still don't have a plan.
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: I have the part where you're alive.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: That's not a plan.
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: It's more than we had yesterday.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: The group clears the execution point with Jeanne alive. For one heartbeat, the square sounds impossibly far away. Then a low, impossible tone rises beneath the city noise.
FIN-B02 — The Broken Horizon.

nodes.title: The Broken Horizon
nodes.location: Rouen — streets beyond Vieux-Marché and the fractured horizon
nodes.summary: After Jeanne is safely rescued, a world-like call guides the party away from the square to a broad final view. There an unknown antagonist deliberately opens a Fracture and crosses it. Hostile fractured pressure remains in the passage's wake. The voice asks the Rookie for help because the world is breaking, and MC chooses pursuit rather than taking a random escape route.

beats.title: The Call
beats.screenAction: Beyond the execution point, the noise of pursuit thins beneath an impossible tone. The sound seems both distant and inside hearing itself, drawing MC toward a quieter route that opens onto a broad view beyond the square.
beats.dialogueIntent: Introduce the world-like voice as a plea or guidance, not prophecy. It uses the current voiced address Rookie and explains nothing about cosmology yet.
beats.result: The party follows the call far enough from the square to see its apparent destination.

script.text: Behind them, Vieux-Marché is still shouting. Ahead, a low tone cuts through the noise without coming from any visible source.
Do you hear that?
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Yeah.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Rookie...
script.speaker: World Voice

script.text: Hear me.
script.speaker: World Voice

script.text: MC turns toward a quieter street. The strange tone strengthens in that direction while the ordinary pursuit noise falls behind.
Where is that coming from?
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: I don't know.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: The route opens into a broader view across Rouen. Something is already waiting at the far edge of it.
Keep Jeanne moving and follow the call away from the square.
The party reaches the sourceward vista.

beats.title: The Figure at the Horizon
beats.screenAction: An unknown figure stands at the far edge of the view and deliberately opens a large refractive Fracture. The figure notices the arriving party, gives no explanation, and crosses through.
beats.dialogueIntent: Reveal deliberate agency behind this portal without naming the main antagonist, defining their form, or explaining motive. The point is that someone chose to open the way.
beats.result: The unknown antagonist crosses the deliberately opened Fracture; the passage remains unstable behind them.

script.text: At the edge of the view, an unknown figure raises one hand. Light folds inward around it instead of appearing by accident.
A broad refractive Fracture opens deliberately. The figure looks back once toward the arriving party.
That one did it.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: The figure steps through the light and vanishes. The Fracture does not close cleanly behind them.
After them.
script.speaker: MC

beats.title: What the Passage Leaves
beats.screenAction: Unstable hostile shapes and pressure spill out around the antagonist-opened passage. They obstruct the route without behaving like ordinary soldiers, forcing the party to protect Jeanne and push toward the still-open Fracture.
beats.dialogueIntent: Keep supernatural pressure as immediate gameplay without calling it Correction, claiming the world wants Jeanne dead, or defining a final creature taxonomy.
beats.result: The party survives the residual fractured pressure and secures a path toward the antagonist-opened Fracture.

script.text: The passage shudders. Hostile shapes peel out of the warped light and close across the route before their bodies can settle into anything familiar.
Those aren't soldiers.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

script.text: They're still in the way.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Then keep Jeanne moving.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Objective: PROTECT JEANNE. Reach the antagonist-opened Fracture.
Fragments of unfamiliar light flash around the route, but the deliberately opened passage remains the only stable direction.

beats.title: Follow
beats.screenAction: As the party reaches the passage, the voice becomes clearer. It says the world is breaking and asks for help. MC chooses to pursue the figure through the path they deliberately opened.
beats.dialogueIntent: Give MC a reason to continue beyond finding home while avoiding chosen-one language. The world asks for help; MC chooses to answer.
beats.result: MC commits to following the unknown antagonist through the Fracture; Jeanne still gets an independent choice before crossing.

script.text: Rookie...
script.speaker: World Voice

script.text: This world is breaking.
script.speaker: World Voice

script.text: I cannot stop them alone.
script.speaker: World Voice

script.text: Please... follow.
script.speaker: World Voice

script.text: That thing opened the way.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: And went through it.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: FIN-N03 — A Road With No Name.

nodes.title: A Road With No Name
nodes.location: Fractured Rouen — edge of the new Fracture
nodes.summary: The antagonist-opened Fracture remains available only briefly. Its destination is unknown, but MC now has a concrete trail and a plea for help rather than a random escape route. MC chooses pursuit; Jeanne is explicitly free to decide whether to follow.

beats.title: The Trail Ahead
beats.screenAction: The Fracture opened by the unknown figure is still active but already narrowing. It shows no readable destination; the only certainty is that the antagonist went through it.
beats.dialogueIntent: Frame the crossing as a chosen pursuit and unanswered responsibility, not a random escape or guaranteed route home.
beats.result: MC decides that the antagonist-opened Fracture is the first real lead worth following; time to choose is short.

script.text: The Fracture hangs across the view as a broad sheet of bent light. It is already beginning to narrow.
I still don't know where it goes.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: But this time you know someone went through it.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Yeah. That's enough.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Then don't stand here admiring it.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

script.text: The edge of the Fracture contracts another step. Whatever path the unknown figure opened will not stay available.

beats.title: Jeanne Chooses
beats.screenAction: MC refuses to decide for Jeanne. Jeanne considers the unknown Fracture and the world behind her, then steps toward the crossing by her own choice. The distortion surges before any additional crossings are confirmed.
beats.dialogueIntent: End Saga I on agency and consequence. Jeanne chooses the pursuit herself. Do not reveal Saga II, guarantee home, identify the antagonist, or confirm which supporting companions cross.
beats.result: MC and Jeanne enter the antagonist-opened Fracture by choice. The scene cuts before confirming which supporting companions also cross; the destination remains unknown.

script.text: You don't have to come.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Jeanne looks back toward Rouen, then at the unstable light.
I know.
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: I don't know what's beyond that light. I know what's behind us.
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: That's not much of a reason.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: It was enough for you.
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: Jeanne steps beside MC. Behind them, the broken street folds again.
Decide fast. It's closing.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: MC and Jeanne enter the bent light. The distortion surges outward across the street before anyone can tell who else it catches.
SAGA I — THE MAID OF FRANCE COMPLETE
Whiteout. The destination is unknown.
